title: Learning engages transient and sustained cellular mechanisms in the human brain
experiments_summary: Twenty-nine healthy right-handed adults (ages 18–36) performed a 5-element motor sequence learning (MSL) task using the nondominant (left) hand, consisting of 15 practice blocks interleaved with 25-second rest periods. All imaging was conducted on a 3T Connectome MRI scanner (300 mT/m gradients) with a 64-channel head coil. Multimodal MRI was acquired in a longitudinal design at three time points: baseline (pre-learning), 30 minutes post-learning, and 24 hours post-learning. Modalities included: (1) multi-shell diffusion MRI (dMRI) with 8 b-values (200–8,000 s/mm²) for DTI and SANDI modeling; (2) T1-weighted structural MRI for hippocampal subfield segmentation via FreeSurfer; and (3) BOLD fMRI acquired during task performance using a block design. Behavioral performance was quantified via intertap intervals and decomposed into micro-online gains (MONGs) and micro-offline gains (MOGs). dMRI preprocessing used FSL and MRtrix3 pipelines (denoising, Gibbs correction, distortion correction, eddy current correction). DTI fitting used FSL's dtifit on the b=1,200 s/mm² shell to generate MD and FA maps. The SANDI model was fit to the full multi-shell data using the SANDI MATLAB toolbox, decomposing the signal into cell-soma fraction (FSOMA), neurite/cell-process fraction (FNEURITE), and extracellular fraction (FEXTRA). For whole-brain DTI analyses, a nonparametric permutation-based F-test with threshold-free cluster enhancement (TFCE) and the Sandwich Estimator (SwE) toolbox was used to identify longitudinal MD changes (FWE-corrected p<0.05, 1,000 permutations). SANDI metrics were then extracted from DTI-defined clusters as ROIs and compared across sessions using repeated-measures ANOVAs with Bonferroni correction. Linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) assessed the relationship between FSOMA and FNEURITE temporal changes (relative to baseline) and behavioral metrics (MOGs, MONGs, overnight offline gains), with time point as a repeated factor and subjects as a random effect. A complementary model-agnostic ROI analysis was performed in anatomically defined hippocampal subfields (head, body, tail) segmented independently of diffusion metrics, where DTI and SANDI metrics were fitted and compared across sessions using repeated-measures ANOVAs. fMRI data were preprocessed in SPM12 with standard steps (motion correction, distortion correction, normalization to MNI152, 8-mm smoothing), and whole-brain GLM analyses identified regions active during task execution versus rest using one-tailed t-tests (FWE-corrected p<0.05). Mean BOLD signal from the four DTI-defined ROIs was also extracted and compared against a resting baseline using one-sample t-tests to confirm functional engagement during learning.
